{{nihongo|'''Sahimeyama Shrine'''|佐毘売山神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iwami Province]].

'''Sahimeyama Shrine''' (さひめやまじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Masuda, Shimane|ar|ماسودا (شيمانه)|azb|ماسودا، شیمانه|bg|Масуда|ce|Масуда (гӀала)|ceb|Masuda|cs|Masuda (Šimane)|de|Masuda|es|Masuda (Shimane)|fa|ماسودا، شیمانه|fi|Masuda|fr|Masuda|gl|Masuda|hu|Maszuda|id|Masuda, Shimane|it|Masuda|ja|益田市|ko|마스다시|mg|Masuda|mzn|ماسودا، شیمانه|nl|Masuda|pl|Masuda|pt|Masuda|ro|Masuda|ru|Масуда (город)|sv|Masuda, Shimane|tg|Масуда|tl|Masuda, Shimane|tr|Masuda|tt|Масуда (шәһәр)|uk|Масуда|ur|ماٹسوڈا، شیمانے|vi|Masuda, Shimane|war|Masuda, Shimane|zh|益田市|zh_classical|益田市|zh_min_nan|Masuda-chhī|zh_yue|益田|qid=Q753731}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}. {{ill|Sahimeyama Shrine|ja|佐毘売山神社 (大田市)|qid=Q11383231|lt=Sahimeyama Shrine}} at {{ill|Iwami Ginzan Silver Mine|ar|منجم إوامي غينزان للفضة|bg|Ивами Гиндзан|ca|Iwami Ginzan|cs|Iwami Ginzan|de|Silberbergwerk Iwami|es|Minas de plata de Iwami Ginzan|eu|Iwami Ginzan-go zilar meategiak|fa|معدن نقره ایوامی|fi|Iwamin hopeakaivos|fr|Iwami Ginzan|gl|Mina de prata Iwami Ginzan|he|איוואמי גינזאן|hr|Iwami Ginzan|hu|Ivami Ginzan ezüstbánya|id|Tambang Perak Iwami Ginzan|it|Iwami Ginzan|ja|石見銀山|ka|იბამი-გინძანი|ko|이와미 은광|mt|Minjiera tal-Fidda ta' Iwami Ginzan|nl|Zilvermijn Iwami Ginzan|no|Iwami Ginzan sølvgruve|pl|Kopalnia Srebra w Iwami Ginzan|pt|Mina de prata de Iwami Ginzan|ru|Ивами Гиндзан|simple|Iwami Ginzan Silver Mine|sk|Iwami Ginzan|sv|Iwami Ginzan|th|เหมืองเงินอิวามิ|tr|Iwami Ginzan Gümüş Madeni|uk|Івамі ґіндзан|vi|Mỏ bạc Iwami Ginzan|zh|石見銀山遺跡及其文化景觀|zh_yue|石見銀山|qid=Q174139}} ({{ill|Ōda, Shimane|Q384796|qid=Q384796}}) is a branch shrine of this shrine.

=== Enshrined deities ===
Its principal deities are {{ill|Kanayama-hiko and Kanayama-hime|es|Kanayamahiko y Kanayamahime|ja|金山彦神|pl|Kanayamahiko|zh|金山毘古神|qid=Q4387856|lt=Kanayamahiko-no-Mikoto and Kanayamahime-no-Mikoto}}. Enshrined in the paired hall are {{ill|Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|Q9285919|qid=Q9285919|lt=Haniyamahime-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Ōyamatsumi|Q386563|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamazumi-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|Q1781862|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohanasakuyahime-no-Mikoto}}; in a separate hall are {{ill|Kuraokami|Q644201|qid=Q644201|lt=Kurakura-no-Kami}} and Hirokuni Oshitake Kanahi Tennō ({{ill|Emperor Ankan|Q241765|qid=Q241765}}).

=== History ===
The origin of its foundation is unknown. At first it stood on the summit of Hirefuri-yama (Sahimeyama), enshrining three goddesses - Kanayamahime, Haniyamahime, and Konohanasakuyahime - and was called “Himeyama Shrine.” “Sahimeyama” is “Himeyama” with the prefix “sa.” In {{ill|Kanpyō (era)|Q1346292|qid=Q1346292}} 5 ({{ill|893|Q24762|qid=Q24762}}), Kanayamahiko-no-Mikoto, a deity of mines, was invited from {{ill|Nangū Taisha|Q704967|qid=Q704967}} in {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}}, and mountain deity Ōyamazumi-no-Mikoto was also enshrined, so it was also called “Gosha Daigongen.” It is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} as “Sahimeyama Shrine, {{ill|Mino District, Shimane|ja|美濃郡|nl|Mino (district)|pt|Distrito de Mino|zh|美濃郡|qid=Q2341285}}, {{ill|Iwami Province|bar|Provinz Iwami|cs|Provincie Iwami|de|Provinz Iwami|es|Provincia de Iwami|fa|ولایت ایوامی|fr|Province d'Iwami|gl|Provincia de Iwami|id|Provinsi Iwami|it|Iwami (provincia)|ja|石見国|ko|이와미국|lt|Ivamio žemė|nl|Iwami (provincie)|pt|Província de Iwami|ru|Ивами (провинция)|simple|Iwami Province|sk|Iwami (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ивами|tr|Iwami (vilayet)|uk|Івамі|wuu|石见国|zh|石見國|zh_min_nan|Iwami-kok|qid=Q1053709}},” and ranked as a small shrine.

In {{ill|Jōji|Q1146153|qid=Q1146153}} 4 ({{ill|1365|Q6190|qid=Q6190}}), a drought struck the area; after prayers for rain on Hirefuri-yama, rain fell, and water deity Kurakura-no-Kami and {{ill|Zaō Gongen|Q10514059|qid=Q10514059}} were merged in from {{ill|Mount Yoshino|Q1036938|qid=Q1036938}} in {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}, after which it also came to be called “Zaō Daigongen.”

In {{ill|Bun'an|Q1193586|qid=Q1193586}} 3 ({{ill|1446|Q6430|qid=Q6430}}), it moved from the summit to the mountainside, and later in {{ill|Manji (era)|Q1145295|qid=Q1145295}} 3 ({{ill|1660|Q7001|qid=Q7001}}), it moved again to the present site.

In Kansei 3 ({{ill|1791|Q7784|qid=Q7784}}), it was renamed to the current shrine name recorded in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō. Due to the Meiji-era {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}, Zaō Gongen as an enshrined deity was changed to Hirokuni Oshitake Kanahi Tennō, regarded as Zaō Gongen’s Buddhist original. In Meiji 5, it was ranked as a village shrine.
